sections.content:
11,050 people

were counted on the census as "podiatrists" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Podiatrists (formerly known as chiropodists) diagnose and treat ailments and abnormalities of the human foot and lower limb, deal with minor infections, injuries and deformities, and conditions resulting from other major health disorders such as diabetes.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "podiatrists" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "podiatrists", 17.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "podiatrists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "podiatrists" included:

  • counsellors
  • bus and coach drivers
  • large goods vehicle drivers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "podiatrists" there were more women than men (75.8% compared with 24.2%).

This means "podiatrists" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 24.2% and women made up 75.8% of "podiatrists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "podiatrists" included:

  • careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists
  • credit controllers
  • finance officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "podiatrists", 11.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (54.8% compared with 45.2%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (56.3%) than an employee (43.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
